classification.difficultyReason: Recover the original value by substituting into the compound depreciation formula and dividing by the four-year multiplier.

content.prompt: Jo bought a four-year old car for $\$20\,880.25$ at its correct depreciated value. If the car has a depreciation rate of $15\%$ p.a., then find the value of the car when it was brand new. Give your answer to the nearest cent.

answer.short:
$\$40\,000.00$

Divide the depreciated value by $(0.85)^4$ to recover the original value.
answer.worked:
Let $P$ be the original value in dollars. Here $R=0.15$ and $n=4$.

$$\begin{align*}A_n&=P(1-R)^n\\20\,880.25&=P(0.85)^4\\P&=\frac{20\,880.25}{(0.85)^4}\\P&=40\,000.\end{align*}$$

The car was worth $\$40\,000.00$ when brand new.
